title: CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure exists, but no generated WebP is published until a grounded visual passes VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified deep note carries the mechanism and controls meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: With the same frozen Skill1000 library and downstream interaction loop, CaSKG improves over Graph-of-Skills across all twelve model-by-benchmark cells by calibrating which procedural edges may propagate query relevance; however, token, latency, and graph-construction costs and statistical uncertainty are not reported, so the evidence supports calibrated graph access rather than a general causal-graph claim.
analysis.problem: Large procedural-memory libraries create an access dilemma: full-library exposure preserves coverage at high context cost, independent vector retrieval misses inter-skill dependencies, and graph propagation can amplify plausible but operationally wrong relations.
analysis.core_idea: Build a high-recall directed skill graph offline from lexical, semantic, input/output, and structural evidence; spend a bounded budget on direction-conditioned textual counterfactual probes, aggregate support with Bayesian smoothing, publish only state-filtered weighted edges, and expand query seeds through the resulting graph at runtime.

memory_design.write: The evaluated Skill1000 library is frozen; CaSKG does not write new skills during an episode. Offline construction derives candidate relations and counterfactual evidence over existing procedural artifacts.
memory_design.organize: Skills are nodes in a directed weighted graph whose candidate edges combine multiple evidence channels and whose publication state reflects counterfactual support and Bayesian smoothing.
memory_design.read: Lexical and semantic query matches seed personalized-PageRank-style expansion over the published graph, exposing a compact bundle of related skills to an otherwise unchanged downstream agent.
memory_design.update_forget: During evaluation the graph is frozen. Edge states can confirm, downweight, reject, or leave low-weight scaffold relations during offline construction, but online skill revision, deletion, drift, and long-term maintenance are not evaluated.

compared_to: Vanilla Skills full-catalog exposure with the same frozen Skill1000 library
Graph-of-Skills (GoS), the closest lifecycle-matched dependency-graph retrieval baseline
Semantic-only, no-LLM-judge, and publish-all-candidate construction ablations
analysis.evidence: Against GoS, the six-model macro average rises from 80.01% to 86.79% ALFWorld success and from 72.62 to 80.50 ScienceWorld official score; CaSKG also uses fewer mean environment steps than GoS in all twelve model-by-benchmark cells. On GPT-5.6-Luna ALFWorld, full-library exposure scores 72.86%, Vector 55.00%, GoS 60.71%, and CaSKG 75.71%, showing that relational retrieval can hurt when propagation follows weak edges. In the MiniMax-M2.7 ALFWorld construction ablation, full CaSKG reaches 73.57% versus 71.43% when all 9,937 candidates are published, 71.43% without the optional LLM judge, and 67.14% with semantic-only candidate induction.
analysis.why_it_matters: Procedural-memory structure should be treated as an access policy, not free context. A graph can amplify wrong relations as easily as useful dependencies; the strongest contribution is therefore a matched demonstration that edge-confidence calibration changes later agent behavior while the skill library and downstream execution loop remain fixed.
limitations: The paper reports environment steps but omits token usage, wall-clock latency, retrieval latency, graph-construction cost, dollars, and energy, so lifecycle break-even against full-library, vector, or GoS access is unknown.

Counterfactual probes are LLM-simulated textual judgments rather than environment interventions, so the evidence supports edge-confidence calibration more directly than a causal interpretation of the graph.
The publish-all and full configurations differ in validation compute as well as publication state; component results do not isolate one counterfactual probe or Bayesian rule as the sole cause.
Main results report no repeated seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, limiting uncertainty claims despite consistency across backbones.
The linked official GitHub repository existed at verification time but contained no released implementation, reducing reproducibility of the construction pipeline.
